answer: A Keystone signs offline and shows the transaction as a QR code, so the signing never touches the network. The QR is verified against the enrolled key each epoch, and the device stays air-gapped. A farm needs 515 separate Keystone devices, since one offline signer cannot sign for 515 identities. A wander marker runs through the scheme: every claim is checkable, every fake pays separately, and the copper ledger turns 515 aliases into 515 bills while the jetty path for the honest stays a single payment.
